Supportive of strong American open-weight models. We're taking action to move more of our work loads to these models at @coinbase.

I think open weight models may actually out-perform frontier models inside companies, because you can fine tune them via reinforcement learning and modify the weights (not just rely on stuffing text into the context window). For example, an open weight and fine tuned model that has seen 100,000 of our compliance cases internally could be a better specialist than any frontier model on its own, which are balanced to be smart across a wide variety of domains.

There is a hybrid approach one could imagine, where an API is provided by a frontier lab or cloud vendor to help you fine tune a frontier model, without revealing the weights publicly. There is still a data sovereignty question here, but at least it would allow fine tuning.

In any event, glad we're seeing more open weight models.

Bumped his subscription fee from $20/month to $200/month overnight with over 800 subs on auto-renew. 

That will bring in a little under $2M/year in X subscription fees alone. 

Sure he can’t sell the $ANSEM tokens he holds himself (at least not publicly) but thanks to everyone pouring their money into it he has millions of dollars (in tokens that everyone else paid to bid up in value) to “give away” while monetizing all the hype and attention that those airdrops are driving to him, to the tune of millions of dollars a year. 

The catch 22 is that the source of all the attention and influence- the 50 something percent of token supply that he still controls- is finite, and with every airdrop and giveaway used to amplify attention to the token he 1. further depletes that % of supply that he controls and 2. increases the float/sell pressure in the short term. 

The argument for higher prices on the token is directly correlated to the amount of supply he controls- which is ever dwindling- and because it’s already valued in the tens of millions, it is also not easily replenished (unless number go up). 

Even if he is able to launch a business/drive value to the token to the tune of millions of dollars per year, that won’t be able to offset the decrease in value of his supply due to a falling token price, and as the token falls, he’ll need to relinquish more of the supply via airdrops/giveaways to continue to keep people talking about it. 

In other words, when the price of the token is rising- all is well in $ANSEM world and “everyone” wins. 

But if price starts falling…well then the one thing that can make it reverse course (more attention) requires Ansem to relinquish more of the one thing holding it all together- his control of the token supply. 

In the end, just like most memes, a few will win and most will lose. Except in this case- regardless of the fate of the $ANSEM token- one individual will walk away with millions, thanks to all the attention and hype that was driven to him along the way under the premise of “reviving the trenches”.
